designationHistory.name: Luquillo Forest Reserve
designationHistory.indexText: President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed the Luquillo Forest Reserve in Puerto Rico.
designationHistory.note: UCSB's '495' is the American Presidency Project's own document number; the Statutes at Large print this as proclamation No. 41 of the 57th Congress.

sources.name: Proclamation of Jan. 17, 1903, 32 Stat. 2029 (govinfo, Statutes at Large)
Forest Service, Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries and National Grasslands: A Chronological Record, 1891-2012 (FS-612), govinfo copy
American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara), Proclamation 495, Establishment of the Luquillo Forest Reserve
Forest History Society, 'The National Forests of the United States' (Appendix I of Davis, ed., Encyclopedia of American Forest and Conservation History, 1983)

designationHistory.name: Luquillo National Forest
designationHistory.indexText: Congress provided that forest reserves would be known as national forests, so the Luquillo Forest Reserve became the Luquillo National Forest.
designationHistory.note: Approved by President Theodore Roosevelt at 9:43 a.m. on Mar. 4, 1907 (the act's approval line). Mar. 4, 1907 was not an inauguration day.

sources.name: Act of Mar. 4, 1907 (Agricultural Appropriation Act), ch. 2907, 34 Stat. 1256, 1269 (govinfo)

designationHistory.name: Caribbean National Forest
designationHistory.indexText: President Franklin D. Roosevelt renamed the Luquillo National Forest the Caribbean National Forest.
designationHistory.note: The 1935 order predates the Federal Register; it is listed in FS-612, Davis and the WPA list, and its text is reproduced by the American Presidency Project.

sources.name: American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara), Executive Order 7059-A, Changing the Name of the Luquillo National Forest

designationHistory.indexText: President George W. Bush renamed the Caribbean National Forest the El Yunque National Forest.
